title: Session-capture staged note (note.json)
description: session-capture-contract.md §3.3 / ADR-0044 §6. The repo-global staging slot written only by the explicit `runtime:context note` invocation (the write itself is the ADR-0035 invariant-1 opt-in). Deliberately per-repo, not per-session: the CLI has no trustworthy session identity, so the staging-time git context below is what lets a consumer see that a note staged on another branch or hours earlier is being republished. The 4096-byte content cap is enforced by the writer in BYTES; the maxLength here is a codepoint-level backstop, not the normative cap.

staged_at.description: UTC instant of THIS staging write. Re-staging identical text refreshes it, and §5's fingerprint note component includes it — so a re-staged note always republishes the slot (settlement of the plan-verify re-staging gap).

host.description: Supplied by the invoking wrapper when known; null when the CLI was invoked bare.

branch.description: Staging-time branch; null on detached HEAD or when the git probe degraded (§6).

head_short.description: Staging-time short HEAD; null on unborn HEAD or probe degradation.

content.description: The staged note verbatim. Writer-enforced 4096-BYTE cap (§4); multi-line allowed here — single-line clamping happens at the entry projection, never at staging.

content_hash.description: sha256 of the exact content bytes; feeds the §5 fingerprint note component together with staged_at.
